issues.description: Constructor parameter order for Meal is inconsistent: the problem statement UML and the solution implementation define the constructor as Meal(String name, String[] ingredients), but the template Meal.java declares the constructor as Meal(String[] ingredients, String name). This mismatch will confuse students, cause the provided example usages in Main (which use Meal(String, String[])) to not compile if uncommented, and make it unclear which signature to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor parameter order consistent across artifacts. Update the template Meal.java constructor signature to public Meal(String name, String[] ingredients) and adjust any template/example usages accordingly (e.g., Main). Alternatively, update the problem statement and solution to match the template if the reversed order was intended, but keeping name first (as in the UML and solution) is recommended to match the documented API.

issues.description: The Problem Statement and Solution define Meal with constructor signature Meal(String name, String[] ingredients) (name first, then ingredients), but the Template's Meal constructor is declared as Meal(String[] ingredients, String name) (parameters reversed). This mismatch (also visible because the Template Main uses the name-first instantiation) creates confusion for students: the example usage in Main and the exercise description do not match the provided constructor signature in the template, forcing students to resolve an unexpected constructor order rather than focus on the task.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the Template Meal constructor signature to public Meal(String name, String[] ingredients) so it matches the Problem Statement and Solution. Alternatively, update the example usages in Main to match the template constructor, but aligning the constructor to name-first is recommended to match the exercise description.
